album_reviews.review:
La Luz's 2024 release has more of their signature sound (spooky, surfy, beautiful fem vox harmonies); this release has more cosmic overtones, and features some heavier influences: the band has been through some roster changes, and frontwoman Shana Cleveland has been recovering from a cancer diagnosis soon after having a kid (she's now cancer-free, fwiw); great, great stuff as always

1. (00:53) ***** Brief trio harmonizing, not really a song, but haunting and optimistic, sunrise-y
2. (4:14) ***** Nasty doomy guitar riffs repeating to start, very mod into vox, so cool "in a strange world"
3. (3:27) ****** Spacey and more lonesome pipey vox; stabby guitars, into more hopeful chorus "I'll be there with you so soon..."; lovely clapping
4. (3:32) ****** Forelorn sing-songy; lovely chattery doot-doot-doot chorus, spooky and lush
5. (3:15) ***** Spooky but hopeful sound, lovely lush chorus, sounds like emerging from cave; funky organ solo
6. (3:24) *** Sideways faux-atonal vox verse; fuller chorus 
7. (3:51) *** Funky intro, mostly instrumental "la la la" chorus, simple but atmospheric
8. (3:04) ***** Doomy intro, into lush, slow doo-wop sugar-sweet dirge... "yep yep yep yep yep" 
9. (3:13) *** Slinkier synthier 80s organ intro, oblique vox, ends up in echoey soup
10. (2:40) **** Torrid drum intro... spacey, fast, reedy, plucked deadpan vox "change is the only law..."
11. (2:00) *** Instrumental; squonky synth plunking intro, simple and repeating 
12. (1:32) **** Very sweet short strummy acoustic ballad, very nice, if not the classic La Luz sound

Hazy, soupy, dreamy psychedelic woozecore: beautiful self-released album (nice to see a major album *not* be on Spotify), this double-album has really got under everyone's skin all year (should have been added/reviewed in the spring, but better late than never). Cindy Lee is the project of Patrick Flegel (they/them), formerly of Women--an act done in drag (btw, I delineated between masculine and feminine vocals in the track reviews, but this is purely about how the vocals present). Anyway, beautiful, dreamy, nostalgic sounds here. Most everything captures this same vibe/timber/mood, but some variation from track to track

DISC 1
1. (5:22) ****** fairly quiet intro for 20+ seconds (completely silent for 5); spidery guitar, dreamy; squonky strings, thumping, accelerates, hits vocals at 2 minutes in; very pretty and bittersweet and hazy
2. (4:10) **** old-timey hazy sounds on radio? into fuzzy guitar, rollicking country-rock in a haze... at 3 min in, becomes gloomy goth fingerpicking with ominous gong sounds til end
3. (3:55) *** bubblegum fuzz sounds, chanting ♂ “baby baby blue” vocals; stony, repetitive
4. (2:46) **** wistful, ♀ vox; distorted, reedy falsetto chorus, glassy, torch song sad, but with buzzy driving strings (?)
5. (3:00) ****** ♀ Sad, half-wailing, half-smirking; really pretty
6. (3:15) **** ♂ Little sad slow folk tune with public restroom acoustics, lingering outro
7. (1:31) ** Short instrumental; Neon electric string section, funk beat
8. (3:43) **** ♀ Mid-slow walking beat with far-away feeling
9. (2:04) ** Sweet guitar strumming; ♂--short, incomplete-feeling
10. (5:13) ***** Hazy co-ed duet sound, wistful and driving with drum-machine sounds, almost cyberpunk; triumphant fresh vibes... sudden clip-out end
11. (1:02) ** Church music interlude + Morricone vibes
12. (4:42) ****** My favorite track, sounds half amusement park, half heaven; angelic ♀ vox glitters over murky, sweet music hall/tango/stew wah-wah guitar, etc, etc; oh god this is so pretty--last minute outro is the sound of heaven
13. (4:24) *** Hypnotic but with a light touch; ♂ vox, 
14. (3:32) **** ♀ slow, high school prom slowness and sadness; expressive and shambolic guitar break
15. (4:04) ** Very slow; ♂, doomy
16. (3:42) **** Instrumental, shimmery and pretty sounds of heavens, strings + more; very simple but very nice
DISC 2
1. (4:22) ***** Slinky, mysterious spy movie sounds; ♀ vox enter at 2 minutes, still slinky and funky
2. (2:56) **** Instrumental, bongos and doomy crunchy chase sequence sounds
3. (6:08) *** Slow hypnotic instrumental opening, ♀ vox at 2 minutes, chanting and oblique and slinky, somewhat atonal and strange
4. (4:39) *** ♂ vox, driving; strange/mysterious/slinky
5. (5:06) ***** Basement-y, ♀ vox, sad torch song turns into weird hopeful prom-my finger-snapping with tape-hiss soup and more
6. (2:57) ***** Sad ♀ vox, beautiful yearning melody, some spanish-inflected guitar
7. (3:33) **** Slow and somewhat warped co-ed duet, strange and distorted in background ways; SUDDEN ending, into->
8. (2:49) **** SUDDEN start (no intro, cut-off); ♀ vox, wistful yearning -- weird synths in bg; SUDDEN ending, into->
9. (4:01) **** sudden start (though not cut-off) ♀ vox, mid-tempo ... some severe guitar feedback midway
10. (3:04) ***** Very "Sleep Walk" guitar instrumental noodling, sweet and surreal
11. (4:48) ***** Sad, yearning ♀ vox, the yearning is so deep here; very sad, pretty
12. (3:29) **** Clearer than usual ♂ vox, hopeful morning sounds, birds chirping and more 
13. (3:50) ***** Funky 60s nightclub bassline, ♀ vox a minute in, muddy and weird and dancy and sad
14. (5:24) ***** Sad fuzzy recording sound, ♂ vox, slow and hypnotic, but affecting, last minute faster
15. (3:13) ***** Sweet, hopeful 50s duet sound, ♀ vox dominates, like the hopeful parts of Twin Peaks
16. (5:25) ***** Instrumental, just the sound of resonant strings, texture of heaven; sudden ending

Reviewed: 2018-05-08
Genre: Jazz
FCCs: none
Review: By 1969, as these newly discovered tapes show, Evans’ approach had solidified: the trio’s repertoire consisted of a number of carefully arranged standards, from which he extracted the last drop of lyricism while draining away any hint of sentimentality, plus a handful of his own compositions. With Eddie Gomez and Marty Morrell, Evans had found once more a rhythm section that questioned, provoked, prodded and scribbled over his best laid plans, and in this relaxed setting they certainly sound like they’re enjoying it.
If You Like: Wynton Kelly, Herbie Hancock
Track Review (favorites denoted by *):
DISC 1
*1/ Our Love Is Here To Stay (4:42) – piano starts strong> uptempo jam> rocking bass solo> uptempo jam begins swinging faster> crescendo end
2/ Sugar Plum (9:43) – piano starts with midtempo solo> midtempo jam> bass solo> piano solo to fade
**3/ Stella By Starlight (6:46) -piano starts> slow jam swings uptempo> bass solo>  spirited piano solo> uptempo jam> crescendo & fade
4/ My Foolish Heart (4:38) – piano starts> slow jam builds to midtempo> piano solo> midtempo jam> mellow crescendo end
***5/ Waltz For Debby (7:57) – piano starts> midtempo jam swings up> piano solo> uptempo jam> swinging bass solo> uptempo jam> swings to fast tempo> quick fade
*6/ ‘Round Midnight (6:37) – piano starts strong & fast>pause> slow jam> piano solo builds to uptempo jam> bass solo> midtempo jam swings back to fast tempo> crescendo end
*7/ The Two Lonely People (8:02) – piano starts with midtempo solo> midtempo jam> piano solo swings uptempo> uptempo jam> bass solo> midtempo jam> crescendo &n fade 
**8/ Who Can I Turn To (When Nobody Needs Me) (7:30) – piano starts strong midtempo & quickly swings into uptempo jam> bass solo> uptempo jam swings to fast tempo> off to the races> lightning fast jam> crescendo end
DISC 2
*9/ Elsa (7:08) – piano starts with a midtempo solo> midtempo jam> piano solo swings up uptempo> uptempo jam> bass solo> midtempo jam> fade
10/ What Are You Doing The Rest Of Your Life (5:39) – bass/piano starts hesitating> slow jam with waves of notes> crescendo end
*11/ Turn Out The Stars (5:03) – piano starts strong & slow> slow jam mellows slightly> piano solo swings into uptempo jam, then mellows to midtempo>slow fade
**12/ Re: Person I Knew (8:51) – piano starts slow, builds into midtempo jam> slowly builds to uptempo jam> bass solo> uptempo jam> slows to fade
13/ Goodbye (2:32) – bass/piano starts> midtempo jam slows to slow tempo> piano solo builds to midtempo jam> crescendo end
*14/ Come Rain And Come Shine (5:05) – piano srarts> midtrempo jam> swings uptempo> piano solo> bass solo>uptempo jam> quick fade
*15/ Very Early (4:45) – piano starts slow> swings into fast tempo jam> bass solo> fast jam> crescendo end
***16/ So What (8:22) – piano starts slow, bass comes in very fast> pause> bass starts> uptempo hesitating jam morphs into swinging  jam> piano solo> uptempo jam> piano solo> uptempo jam> pause> bass solo racks out with drums> pause> uptempo jam> quick fade
17/ Midnight Mood (4:44) – piano starts> midtempo jam> piano solo swings into uptempo jam, then mellows to midtempo> crescendo end
1*8/ Polkadots And Moonbeams (3:54) - piano starts strong & slow, swings to midtempo jam, then uptempo> piano solo> fade
